Convert Between NIW/NIX Hyperparameters and Expected/Marginal Moments

Source: R/S7-niw-nix-conversions.R
get_expected_Sigma_from_S.Rd

Functions to convert between conjugate Normal-Inverse-Wishart (NIW) or Normal-Inverse-Chi-Squared (NIX) hyperparameters (\(m, S\)) and the expected or marginal distribution moments (\(\mu, \Sigma\)) (see Murphy 2012 p. 134) .

Usage

get_expected_Sigma_from_S(S, nu)

get_S_from_expected_Sigma(Sigma, nu)

get_marginal_Sigma_from_S(S, nu, kappa)

get_expected_mu_from_m(m)

get_m_from_expected_mu(mu)

Arguments

S

Scatter matrix \(S\) (numeric matrix, scalar, or list of matrices).

nu

Strength of belief (pseudocount) about \(\Sigma\) (\(\nu > D + 1\)).

Sigma

Expected category covariance matrix \(\Sigma\) (numeric matrix, scalar, or list of matrices).

kappa

Strength of belief (pseudocount) about \(\mu\).

m

Location hyperparameter \(m\) (numeric vector, matrix, or list).

mu

Expected category mean vector \(\mu\) (numeric vector, matrix, or list).

Value

For get_expected_Sigma_from_S, the expected covariance matrix \(\Sigma = S / (\nu - D - 1)\). For get_S_from_expected_Sigma, the scatter matrix \(S = \Sigma \cdot (\nu - D - 1)\). For get_marginal_Sigma_from_S, the marginal category covariance matrix \(\Sigma = (\kappa + 1) / \kappa \cdot S / (\nu - D - 1)\). For get_expected_mu_from_m and get_m_from_expected_mu, the mean vector or location hyperparameter.

Details

Under the NIW model with \(D\) dimensions, scatter matrix \(S\), and degrees of freedom / pseudocounts \(\nu > D + 1\), the expected covariance matrix is: $$\Sigma = \frac{S}{\nu - D - 1}$$ Conversely, the scatter matrix is obtained from \(\Sigma\) by: $$S = \Sigma \cdot (\nu - D - 1)$$. For conjugate NIW and NIX models, the expected mean \(\mu\) is identically equal to the location parameter \(m\): $$\mu = m$$

References

Murphy KP (2012). Machine learning: a probabilistic perspective. MIT Press.

See also

get_expected_sigma, get_expected_mu

Examples

# 2D example
S <- matrix(c(4, 1, 1, 3), nrow = 2)
nu <- 10
kappa <- 5

# Convert scatter matrix to expected covariance matrix (D = 2)
Sigma <- get_expected_Sigma_from_S(S, nu = nu)
Sigma
#>           [,1]      [,2]
#> [1,] 0.5714286 0.1428571
#> [2,] 0.1428571 0.4285714

# Convert expected covariance matrix back to scatter matrix
get_S_from_expected_Sigma(Sigma, nu = nu)
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> [1,]    4    1
#> [2,]    1    3

# Marginal covariance matrix
get_marginal_Sigma_from_S(S, nu = nu, kappa = kappa)
#> [1] 0.6857143

# Mean and location conversions
m <- c(0, 1)
mu <- get_expected_mu_from_m(m)
get_m_from_expected_mu(mu)
#> [1] 0 1
